 :JUDGMENT:

The petitioners have preferred this petition U/s. 166 of Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation of sum of Rs.50,00,000/.
2.
Brief facts of the averments of the petition are as under:
That the petitioner No.1 is the wife and petitioners No.2 and 3 are the children of Batchu Suryaprasad

. On 27.06.2019, the said Batchu Suryaprasad was crossing the road opposite to the Raagigudda Anjaneya Temple of 2 nd phase, J.P. Nagar, near South End cross, cautiously observing all the traffic rules.

During that time, the driver of Autorickshaw bearing Reg.
No.KA05AD9065 driven the same at a very high speed in a rash and negligent manner came from 46th cross road towards temple's road and dashed to Mr. Batchu Suryaprasad.
Due to the impact, the said person fell down and sustained severe injury to his head and to the other parts of his body.
3. Immediately he was shifted to NIMHANS Hospital and thereafter to Apollo Hospital, where he was treated as an inpatient.
On account of the inconvenience to the family members to stay at Bengaluru to continue treatment, the injured was taken to Pulse Hospital of Kakinada of Andhra Pradesh.

sentences.text: While he was taking treatment in the hospital, on 04.07.2019 at about 7.45 AM, he succumbed.

2 4. According to the petitioners, prior to the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy and was drawing handsome salary of Rs.50,000/ per month.
He was also an income tax payee.
As a result of death of the husband and father of petitioners herein they being the dependents have suffered severe mental agony and have last the love and affection of the deceased.
The deceased was aged 53 years old at the time of his death.

5. In connection with the incident, the Jayanagar Traffic Police have registered a case in Crime No.37/2019 against the driver of Autorickshaw bearing Reg. No.KA05AD9056 for the offences punishable U/s.279, 337 and 304A of IPC.
The respondent No.1 is the insurer of the said vehicle and respondent No.2 is the RC owner of the vehicle and as such they are jointly and severally liable to compensate the petitioners.
With all these averments, the petitioners pray to allow the petition and to grant the relief.

6. Upon service of notice on the respondents, the respondents made appearance through their respective learned advocates and have contested the petition by filing their respective statement of objections in detail.
7. In the objection filed by respondent No.1, it has denied the entire averments made in the petition as false and frivolous.
According to it, the policy number mentioned in the petition in respect of the offending vehicle in question has not been issued by it.

In addition to this, it is also contended that,
the respondent No.1 Company has not issued any policy in respect of the offending vehicle.

As such,
there exists no contract between the respondent No.1 and 2 in respect of the offending vehicle.
8. This respondent denied the occurrence of accident on 27.06.2019 and also denied the involvement of offending vehicle in the said accident.

9. This respondent further denies the age, occupation of the deceased and also contends that to make wrongful gain, the petitioners have come up with the frivolous petition stating that, they have incurred such amount of expenses as stated in the petition to perform the last rituals of the deceased.

According to it, the compensation claimed by the petitioners is exorbitant and this respondent has not issued any policy in respect of the offending vehicle, it is not liable for any acts done by the respondent No.2 and as such cannot be held liable to pay compensation as claimed.
10. Respondent No.2 in her statement of objections denied the petition averments as false and frivolous.
According to her, she admits that she is the owner of offending Autorickshaw vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA05AD9056.
She states that, the said vehicle was duly insured with the respondent No.1 under Policy certificate cum policy schedule No.OG1817011831 00000407 and same was valid from 11072018 to 10.07.2019.
She also contends that, the driver of the offending vehicle had valid and effective driving license as on the date of the occurrence of accident.

11. She further contends that on the fatal day, the driver of offending vehicle was cautiously,
following all the traffic rules and regulations driving the offending vehicle on the correct side of the road.
However, as a result of sole negligence on the part of the deceased, who rushed to the road, the accident occurred.
Had the deceased was cautious, he could have avoided the accident.

12. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues were framed:

Whether the petitioners prove that, they are the legal representatives of the deceased?

Late Batchu Venkatarao died due to the injuries sustained by him in an accident occurred on 27.06.2019 at about 11.45 a.m to 12.00 p.m, opposite to Ragigudda Anjaneya Temple of 2nd phase of J.P. If so, how much and from whom?

My findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative,.
Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.4 : As per final order for the following:
REASONS 19. Issue No.1: Factual matrix of the case has been already narrated in brief in the above paragraphs.
According to the petitioners, the petitioner No.1 is the wife and petitioner No.2 and 3 are the children of late Batchu Suryaprasad.
Further, the relationship of the petitioners with that of the deceased has remained undisputed.

Apart from that, the oral evidence given by PW.1 with regard to B. Annapurna Alias Batchu Annapurna vs Bajaj All Gen Ins Co Ltd on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142545819/

sentences.text: her relationship with the deceased and the relationship of the deceased with the other petitioners corroborates the documentary evidence placed as per Ex.P.19 to Ex.P.22.

As the contents of Ex.P.19 reflects that the petitioner No.1 herein is the wife of late Bitchu Suryaprasad and the contents of Ex.P.20 and Ex.P.21 depicts that the petitioners No.2 and 3 are the children of late Bitchu Suryaprasad.
Apart from that, the police records furnished on hand also justify the fact that the petitioners are the legal representatives of the deceased.
As per the recitals of Ex.P.11, the petitioners herein are considered as the legal representatives of the deceased.

As there is no serious dispute regarding this aspect as the documents corroborates the oral evidence of PW.1 regarding the fact that the petitioners herein are the legal representatives of the deceased, it is suffice to hold that the petitioners have proved the issue No.1.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
20. Issue No.2:

According to the petitioners, the deceased along with some of his family members had visited the Ragigudda Anjaneya Temple situated at 2nd phase of J.P. Nagar, Bengaluru on 27.06.2019 in a Car which belongs to one of the son of the petitioners.

According to them, after coming out from the temple, while deceased was proceeding towards parking area of the said car,
the offending vehicle i.e., Autorickshaw bearing Reg. No.KA05AD9056 which was driven from 46 th cross road by it's driver in a rash and negligent manner came and hit to Bitchu Suryaprasad.

On account of such negligence on the part of driver of the Autorickshaw, Bitchu Suryaprasad sustained severe injuries on his head and to the other parts of body, who later succumbed on 04.07.2019.
21.
The fact that the Respondent No.2 is the RC owner of offending vehicle remained undisputed in this case.
The document Ex.R.1 justifies the said fact.

Though the respondent No.1 denied regarding the involvement of offending vehicle in the alleged accident, the documentary evidence placed on hand by the petitioners as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.4 and the spot sketch Ex.P.6 to Ex.P.8 would justify the involvement of the vehicle in the accident.
The documents spot sketch, Ex

.P.6 to Ex.P.8 and Ex.P.15 would justify the fact of the involvement of the offending vehicle in the alleged accident on 27.06.2019.
22.
Having considered the provision under which, the claimants have preferred this petition, law mandates proof of negligence on the part of the driver of offending vehicle.
It is needless to mention that in the case before MACT, the strict proof of negligence is not necessary.
It is suffice if the petitioners/claimants probabalise their case in support of evidence which they rely upon.
With these observations let us now scrutinize the oral as well as documentary evidence placed on hand by the respective parties.
The evidence given by PW.1 reiterates the averments made in the petition.
Wherein, she has alleged regarding the negligence on the part of driver of Autorickshaw which resulted in occurrence of Road Traffic Accident on 27.06.2019.

Though she has been cross examined at length by learned advocate for the petitioner and by the learned advocate for respondent No.1 and respondent No.2 the evidence deposed by PW.1 regarding the fact of the involvement of vehicle and regarding the alleged negligence on the part of the driver of the offending Autorickshaw remained unshaken.
Apart from that during her evidence, the respondent No.2 has stated that on 27.06.2019, the offending vehicle which stands in her name was driven by her husband by name Mr.Dattakumar.
Further, she has stated that accident did not occurred on account of any negligence on the part of her husband.

sentences.text: It is pertinent to note that the respondent No.2 not taken any pain to get the driver of offending vehicle examined on her behalf to disprove the allegations of negligence.
Such being the case, this Court has to rely upon the police papers.

It is an undisputed aspect that based on the first information of Konaraja Rao, the Jayanagar Traffic Police have registered a case in Cr.No.37/2019 on 27.06.2019 against the driver of offending Autorickshaw in question.

It is also an undisputed fact that subsequently one more FIR has been registered on 04.07.2019 before the Kakenal Police Station under FIR No.182/1019 based on the complaint lodged by the petitioner No.2 herein wherein, the allegations are made against the driver of offending Autorickshaw in question.
24.

It is also evident from the record that the I.O. of Jayanagar Traffic Police Station having taken up thorough investigation has issued notice to the respondent No.2 herein as per Ex.P.6 and the respondent No.2 has given reply to the said notice as per Ex.P.7.

If consideration is given to Ex.P.6 and Ex.P.7, it is clear that the respondent No.2 has admitted of the fact that as on the date of occurrence of accident, the offending vehicle in question was driven by her husband, who is none other than the accused person as per the chargesheet submitted by the I.O.

It is also evident from the records that till date, neither the respondent No.2 nor the accused have questioned the charge sheet which is marked as Ex.P.15.
25.

Upon careful consideration of the entire case papers, it is noticed by the tribunal that the document which is marked as Ex.P.5. Spot Mahazar is pertaining to the Crime No.38/2019 which is not the Crime number connected to this petition.
As such, the said spot mahazar will not come to the aid of the petitioners.
Further there is no impediment to refer the document ie; the spot sketch which clearly discloses the occurrence of accident.
Same would also reveals that had the driver of Autorickshaw driven the same cautiously, he could have avoided the occurrence of accident.

In addition to all these observations, it is also important to note that during her cross examination,
RW.1 has categorically admitted of the fact that the offending vehicle in question was driven by her husband, who is accused in CR. No.37/2019.
All these facts constitute that Batchu Suryaprasad sustained injuries as a result of negligence on the part of the driver of Autorickshaw in question in a road traffic occurred on 27.06.2019.
Upon careful consideration of case papers, it is clear that there is no dispute with regard to the fact of death of Batchu Surya Prasad.
The documents Ex.P.10 to Ex.P.15 and Ex.P.18 justify the fact of death of Batchu Surya Prasad on 04.07.2019 while he was under treatment at Pulse Hospital.

26. The other documents placed on hand, i.e., Ex.P.16 and Ex.P.17 would justify the fact that on the alleged history of road traffic accident occurred on 27.06.2019 at around 12.00 noon near Ragigudda Anjaneya Temple of Bengaluru Mr.Batchu Suryaprasad was admitted to the Apollo Hospital of Bengaluru on 27.06.2019 and he got discharged against the medical advice on 01.07.2019.

If the observations made regarding the injuries sustained by him are considered along with the cause of death mentioned in Ex.P.18 discharge summary, same clearly establishes the fact that Batchu Suryaprasad died on 04.07.2019.
Several suggestions have been made to PW.1 and PW.2 during their crossexamination regarding the cause of death of Batchu Suryaprasad.
However, nothing worth to discredit the evidence has been elicited.

As such, this Court is of the opinion that the Batchu Suryaprasad succumbed as the result of injuries sustained by him in road traffic accident occurred on 27.06.2019 due to the rash and negligent driving of the Autorickshaw B. With all these observations, this Tribunal is of the view that with the aid of the evidence the petitioners have proved this issue and accordingly Issue No.2 is answered in the Affirmative.
27. Issue No.3 :

From the overall observations made supra, while giving findings on issue No.1 and 2, the petitioners are entitled for compensation and to ascertain the quantum of compensation, it is necessary to consider the age of deceased.
The number of dependents which he has left behind him as his legal representatives, avocation of the deceased, the income of deceased before his death.
In the petition, the petitioners have stated that, Batchu Suryaprasad was 53 years old when he succumbed to the injuries.
The document Ex.P.22 i.e., the notarized copy of Aadhar Card of deceased corroborates the age of deceased as 53 years.
The medical records Ex.P.16, Ex.P.17 discloses the age of deceased as 52 years.
Accordingly, the age of deceased considered at 53 years for the purpose of assessment of compensation.

28. According to the petitioners, the deceased was drawing a salary of sum of Rs.50,000/ per month from his avocation as the Manager at Home Sai Marketing Agencies and he was also an income tax payee.
To prove this aspect the petitioners have placed reliance on Ex.P.25 and Ex.P.26.
Upon careful consideration of these documents, it is clear that Batchu Suryaprasad was working as a General Manager prior to the fatal incident.
The careful scrutiny of documents Ex.P.25 and Ex.P.26 gives clear picture regarding the income of the deceased.
Ex.P.25 is of the assessment year 2017 2018, Ex.P.26 is of the assessment year 201819 and 2020, the date of occurrence of accident is on 27.06.2019.

Hence, if the income of the deceased as on that year of occurrence of accident is taken into consideration, he was drawing a gross salary of Rs.4,10,153/ per annum, if same is reduced to 12 month, income of deceased per month is considered at Rs.34,000/ per month.
29. During the crossexamination of PW.1, suggestions were made that the deceased was not having any income.
Same is categorically denied by PW.1.

Even regarding the age, it was suggested that deceased was of the age of 6065 years same has been denied by PW.1.
30.
With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioners are entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF CONSORTIUM, COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF ESTATE, COMPENSATION TOWARDS FUNERAL EXPENSES:
31.
The deceased has left behind him, his wife and his sons.
Hence, the Petitioner No.1 to 3 are considered as dependents.

At this juncture, I would like to go through principles laid down in the decision reported in Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others) wherein Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that : "Loss of estate has to be compensated by awarding Rupees 15,000/, loss of consortium should be Rupees 40,000/ and funeral expenses should be Rupees 15,000/".

As this Court has already observed that the Petitioner No.1 is the wife, Petitioner No.2 and 3 are the sons of the deceased Batchu Suryaprasad, the Petitioners are entitled for a sum of Rupees 44,000/ each towards loss of consortium and Rupees 16,500/ collectively towards loss of estate and Rupees 16,500/ collectively towards funeral expenses.

II. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF LOVE AND AFFECTION,
32.
Petitioner No.1 is the wife and she lost her husband's love and care in her young age, Petitioner No.2 and 3 are the sons of the deceased and they have lost their father's love and care.

Bearing in mind the relationship of the Petitioners with the deceased, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.50,000/ collectively under this head would be just and reasonable.
III. COMPENSATION TOWARDS TRANSPORTATION OF DEAD BODY:
33. The Petitioners might have spent some amount towards transportation of body of the deceased.
Hence, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.10,000/ collectively under this head would be just and reasonable.
IV. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF DEPENDANCY:
34. It is pertinent to note here that as per the detailed discussion as made supra, the income of the deceased was notionally fixed at Rs.34,000/ p.m.

Whether addition on account of future prospects is admissible where minimum income is determined on guesswork in absence of proof of income Held:

Therefore, the income of the deceased comes to Rs.37,400/ p.m. (Rs.34,000/ + Rs.3,400/).
Further, as per the principles laid down in decision reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 (Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another) the multiplier applicable is 11.

sentences.text: In Sarla Verma's case, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has held that where the number of dependent of family members is 2 to 3, 1/3 rd of the income of the deceased may be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.

After deducting 1/3rd towards his personal expenses in Rs.37,400/ it comes to Rs.24,933/
(37,400/ - 12,467) and multiplier applied is 11 which comes to Rs.32,91,156/ (24,933 x 12 =
2,99,196, Rs.2,99,196 x 11 = Rs.32,91,156/).
